opinions.name: Muse
opinions.point: easier than any custom setup, trivial cost
opinions.quote: Muse and cursor. It beats every custom setup I had by far on ease of use. The cost is trivial.

opinions.name: Cursor
opinions.point: easier than any custom setup, trivial cost
opinions.quote: Muse and cursor. It beats every custom setup I had by far on ease of use. The cost is trivial.

opinions.name: Qwen
opinions.point: capable locally, too limited to overbuild
opinions.quote: I have a 4090 which runs Qwen3.8-27b q4 fine with 180k ctx at q8. The model is capable enough to do things, but dumb enough to not be able to build elaborate nonsense like the bigger models love to do

opinions.name: Juggler
opinions.point: good control and insight, but feels vibecoded
opinions.quote: I'm using https://github.com/juggler-ai/juggler which is alright. It could be a bit less vibecoded… but, generally, the opinions shaping it seem decent, and I like just how much control over and insight into what happens it gives you.

opinions.name: OpenCode
opinions.point: a total mess
opinions.quote: I initially tried OpenCode, and, holy hell, what a mess. Do not ever use OpenCode.

opinions.name: Goose
opinions.point: too agentic for their taste
opinions.quote: I initially tried OpenCode, and, holy hell, what a mess… I also tried goose but it was too agentic for my taste.

opinions.name: DeepSeek
opinions.point: produced working PCBs with minimal prompting
opinions.quote: DeepSeek Flash with kicad + autorouting churned out a couple of working PCBs with minimal prompting, and customized ZMK itself for some custom input devices. At least for casual stuff this is a solved problem

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: drives real TV, but misses device-only issues
opinions.quote: I've been building a Samsung TV app with Claude Code, and the agent drives the real TV over the network… What it can't do is notice the things only the device shows you.

opinions.name: Anthropic API
opinions.point: no other models seem reasonable since Anthropic 5.5
opinions.quote: Yes, Anthropic models usually, at work. Pay as you go API… Since the Anthropic 5.5 models none [of the alternatives] seem reasonable to use any longer (for now at least)

opinions.name: Aider
opinions.point: failed to read context; manual file loading
opinions.quote: Tried Aider early on and it failed to even read its initial context… I dropped it dead after that - unusable if you need me to specifically "load" and point our files. That's not agentic coding, sorry.

opinions.name: Gemma
opinions.point: local models unusable on the work codebase
opinions.quote: Used `pi` w/ local models (some gemma and qwen that'd run on my hardware. nothing usable w/ the work code base - or much anything for that matter

opinions.name: Qwen
opinions.point: local models unusable on the work codebase
opinions.quote: Used `pi` w/ local models (some gemma and qwen that'd run on my hardware. nothing usable w/ the work code base - or much anything for that matter

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: best for large projects, manages many subagents
opinions.quote: For very large projects I've found Claude Code to be the best -- it can very easily manage many subagents.

opinions.name: OpenClaw
opinions.point: couldn't find great use cases
opinions.quote: I've tried OpenClaw, Hermes, Dots, and Muse. I really just haven't found great use cases for these tools

opinions.name: Hermes Agent
opinions.point: couldn't find great use cases
opinions.quote: I've tried OpenClaw, Hermes, Dots, and Muse. I really just haven't found great use cases for these tools

opinions.name: Dots
opinions.point: couldn't find great use cases
opinions.quote: I've tried OpenClaw, Hermes, Dots, and Muse. I really just haven't found great use cases for these tools

opinions.name: Muse
opinions.point: couldn't find great use cases
opinions.quote: I've tried OpenClaw, Hermes, Dots, and Muse. I really just haven't found great use cases for these tools

opinions.name: Custom orchestration
opinions.point: most productive and fun ever, and safe
opinions.quote: [With my custom nix-defined workflows,] I never was able to get so much stuff done and had so much fun getting a project build. And fucking safe - no more fear when updating dependencies.

opinions.name: GLM
opinions.point: taking over the work Codex was meant for
opinions.quote: Probably going to drop Codex soon, GLM is gradually taking on what I intended it for.

opinions.name: Parakeet
opinions.point: way better than Whisper for voice input
opinions.quote: So I made my own. Including patching onnx myself to run parakeet model (way better than whisper)

opinions.name: Hermes Agent
opinions.point: shut down over security concerns
opinions.quote: also killed my hermes web setup (also via talescale) for security reasons. not interested in having something online like that with all the vulns popping up

opinions.name: Hermes Agent
opinions.point: fun for automation, but chat gateways buggy
opinions.quote: Just Hermes… - Fun at home, build, automate, disabled gateways for online chatting becauese of bugs

opinions.name: Claude
opinions.point: too expensive for personal use
opinions.quote: Hermes, OpenRouter, . No Claude/Codex sub too expensive. Use them at work instead.

opinions.name: ChatGPT / Codex
opinions.point: too expensive for personal use
opinions.quote: Hermes, OpenRouter, . No Claude/Codex sub too expensive. Use them at work instead.

opinions.name: OpenRouter
opinions.point: nice alternative models, but fewer tokens
opinions.quote: Previously yes (esp. to try out new models on OpenRouter… Wrote about them on my blog, seemed like nice alternatives to OpenAI and Ant, but didn't give me as many tokens

opinions.name: OpenCode
opinions.point: nice CLI, barebones web and desktop UI
opinions.quote: also tried out OpenCode (really nice CLI, but barebones web UI/desktop versions)

opinions.name: Paseo
opinions.point: pleasant, but sub-agent status updates hung
opinions.quote: additional ADEs like Paseo (really pleasant, but sub-agent status updates hanged sometimes)

opinions.name: Kepler
opinions.point: cool ticketing integration, unpleasant UI
opinions.quote: Kepler (cool ticketing system integration, but the UI wasn't very pleasant), before just going back to the two in the end.

opinions.name: Git worktrees
opinions.point: worktrees are all you need for parallel work
opinions.quote: near-SOTA models are good enough to automate long form work and work in parallel well enough, all you need are Git worktrees and a decent OS environment to work in.

opinions.name: Qwen
opinions.point: struggled on old GPU, not very useful
opinions.quote: I tried a local Qwen model but my poor old 1660 Ti did not enjoy it, and it wasn't all that useful.

opinions.name: ChatGPT / Codex
opinions.point: good at features and research, token efficient
opinions.quote: Codex is better at feature implementation and research from what I've found… GPT 6.1 Sol is very token efficient that I pretty much never run out before the end of the week anyways.

opinions.name: Claude
opinions.point: better at frontend and debugging
opinions.quote: In general, Claude's better at frontend and debug and Codex is better at feature implementation and research from what I've found, which is why I have both.

opinions.name: ChatGPT / Codex
opinions.point: 5.6-Sol reliable enough to stop supervising
opinions.quote: That changed wth 5.6-Sol and a handful of skill files. I stopped needing to watch closely to keep it from fucking up the codebase. With the right request, that combination will get the job done 9/10 times.

opinions.name: Custom orchestration
opinions.point: custom solutions are cheap and fit exactly
opinions.quote: So I have a custom solution in place to manage a handful of agents… Custom solutions are so cheap and easy now... it's really hard to put up with solutions that are only mostly right for the job.

opinions.name: Claude
opinions.point: can't use own client without API pricing
opinions.quote: With Anthropic, you cannot access their inference servers without going through one their client software or paying the API pricing. It is really annoying

opinions.name: ChatGPT / Codex
opinions.point: allows using subscription from any client
opinions.quote: OpenAI allows you to do that, so I have a proxy running on my computer which connects to OpenAI's servers… with the requests counting towards my subscription.

opinions.name: OpenRouter
opinions.point: great product for exploring new models
opinions.quote: I also have an OpenRouter account, I use it regularly but mostly to explore new models… OpenRouter has a great product and there is so much possiblity in this space.

opinions.name: Chat UI (web/app)
opinions.point: web version handy, desktop app too heavy
opinions.quote: I either use the web-based version of ChatGPT for quick questions and analytical work (the desktop version is unnecessarily heavy)

opinions.name: Zed
opinions.point: prefers IDE with agents added on
opinions.quote: For coding, I mostly use Zed. I like the traditional development environment and tooling… I prefer an IDE on top of which agents were added.

opinions.name: OpenCode
opinions.point: OpenCode Web has improved, good for scripting
opinions.quote: OpenCode Web has evolved a lot, I have been using it for quick scripting as well.

opinions.name: Codex
opinions.point: liked most, until bugs and the daemon
opinions.quote: I've personally used OpenCode, Claude Code and Codex and of those, I liked Codex the most, till bugs kept on accumulating and they started doing all kinds of shit like that daemon recently.

opinions.name: 3code
opinions.point: small, simple, built-in sandbox, responsive author
opinions.quote: I now switched to https://github.com/capocasa/3code which is a small, simple agent harness but with built-in sandbox… I really like this one, plus the author is very responsive to feedback

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: all you need
opinions.quote: Claude code is all you need

opinions.name: Qwen
opinions.point: runs four concurrent agents on low power
opinions.quote: I am running Qwen Flash Next on Strix Halo with Halogen inference server. This is great setup that can get you 4 concurrent agents for 300W of power

opinions.name: Halogen
opinions.point: runs four concurrent agents on low power
opinions.quote: I am running Qwen Flash Next on Strix Halo with Halogen inference server. This is great setup that can get you 4 concurrent agents for 300W of power with 1k prefill and 30-80tk/s decode.

opinions.name: MLX
opinions.point: really nice for music and pictures
opinions.quote: For music, pictures, etc. MLX-Serve is all I use, with the recommended models. It's really nice.

opinions.name: Perplexity
opinions.point: loves it, but Computer is expensive
opinions.quote: I absolutely love Perplexity. This is by far the AI produce I use the most… It's a little bit sad that they are forcing people to use Perplexity Computer, because it's so expensive. But it works incredibly well.

opinions.name: Comet
opinions.point: indispensable for agentic web browsing
opinions.quote: For agentic web browsing, I can't live without Comet anymore. So many websites are painful to use… So, I frequently just ask Comet to do it for me.

opinions.name: NBClaw
opinions.point: initially exciting, now mostly just summaries
opinions.quote: As for an OpenClaw-like tool, I'm using NBClaw. I was initially very excited about it… But eventually, I used it less and less. Nowadays, I still enjoy the fact that it's sending me a summary of cool things

opinions.name: Custom assistant
opinions.point: rarely so inspired by a project
opinions.quote: I've made a multiplayer environment for me and a few friends, where we can prompt (currently three) emergents… I've rarely been so inspired by a project.

opinions.name: Muse
opinions.point: would never use it as a personal agent
opinions.quote: I would never use Muse, Grok Bot, etc as a personal agent.

opinions.name: Grok bot
opinions.point: would never use it as a personal agent
opinions.quote: I would never use Muse, Grok Bot, etc as a personal agent.

opinions.name: Parakeet
opinions.point: awesome local voice-to-text
opinions.quote: Mostly local voice-to-text w/Parakeet Unified EN 0.6B via Handy[0] (awesome; use it!). Not for coding, but for note taking, AI interfacing, and general typing reduction and RSI avoidance.

opinions.name: Pi
opinions.point: harness interfaces don't fit their work
opinions.quote: I tried Pi and after much kerfuffle I don't like any of the harness interfaces. I find the type of work I do they are not very useful

opinions.name: maki
opinions.point: a great harness
opinions.quote: different harnesses depending on the task, maki is great one, but I use others

opinions.name: Herdr
opinions.point: never clicked
opinions.quote: I tried most of the tools like herdr or paseo or desktop clients but they never clicked with me

opinions.name: Paseo
opinions.point: never clicked
opinions.quote: I tried most of the tools like herdr or paseo or desktop clients but they never clicked with me

opinions.name: OpenClaw
opinions.point: powerful and fun, but plumbing is a chore
opinions.quote: Openclaw is the answer to question "do X if Y happens"… It is a very powerful model I am having lots of fun with it. the plumbing is a chore though

opinions.name: Cursor
opinions.point: happy until forced to use Grok
opinions.quote: Been using Cursor for a long time and happy with it until they started to force Grok down our throats. I was happy with Composer 2.

opinions.name: Cursor
opinions.point: pushed Grok on users; left
opinions.quote: I've switched out of Cursor because A. they've been bullying us into using grok for everything

opinions.name: OpenCode Go/Zen
opinions.point: $40 tier usually enough for the month
opinions.quote: Besides my Opencode GO subscription, I sometimes add a few bucks to use Zen. It's rare: my USD40 is usually fine for the month.

opinions.name: Qwen
opinions.point: local model not useful on shared laptop
opinions.quote: I have a Qwen model available on my Mac (M1 PRO 64GB) but haven't found it to be useful, as I need my laptop for everything else

opinions.name: GLM
opinions.point: incredible tool caller, insufferable prose
opinions.quote: GLM 5.3 Flash and Deepseek 4.1 Flash do most of the work for my personal stuff… GLM, Qwen and Deepseek are incredible tool callers, but their prose is insufferable.

opinions.name: DeepSeek
opinions.point: incredible tool caller, insufferable prose
opinions.quote: GLM 5.3 Flash and Deepseek 4.1 Flash do most of the work for my personal stuff… GLM, Qwen and Deepseek are incredible tool callers, but their prose is insufferable.

opinions.name: GPT Luna
opinions.point: cheap and communicates much better
opinions.quote: I've been using GPT Luna 6 a lot because it's currently cheap as hell… I find that Luna communicates MUCH better than the Chinese models

opinions.name: Hermes Agent
opinions.point: generally happy, but unstable with regressions
opinions.quote: 5) Hermes. Generally happy with it - despite it being extremely unstable between updates, with frequent regressions, weird UI bugs and half assed features (bot mode, anyone?).

opinions.name: Codex
opinions.point: became unwakable in multi-agent setup
opinions.quote: I am still refining how they all communicate, currently codex became unwakable at some point while claude can be woken with a message just fine.

opinions.name: Claude
opinions.point: amazing speed and code quality, but overwhelming
opinions.quote: I have a Claude Code pro subscription, and mostly have Opus as a thinking buddy… I mean the speed is amazing, the code quality is also amazing, but the amount of information I get to process is just insane

opinions.name: Mistral
opinions.point: falls short of Claude Opus
opinions.quote: For the company… we have a Mistral Team subscription, I find it hard to work with anything other than Claude Opus, I really force myself to do it but I often think: Pff, Opus would have gotten this right.

opinions.name: Hermes Agent
opinions.point: handy automations and searchable notes, cheap
opinions.quote: I also have HermesAgent on a nuc here in front of me, it makes small automations… stores notes and articles with I can interrogate as a "body of work" <- love that btw
